question: to the Commission Kostas Papadakis (NI) Subject:

In a period of adjustment towards the ‘war economy’, the alignment of science and research with the pursuits of the capitalist economy is being strengthened, in order to shield EU capital against the possibility of a generalised imperialist war. In its interim evaluation of ‘Horizon Europe’, the EU allocated a huge amount of money to research aimed at developing ‘dual-use’ technologies, while the strategy will be expanded in the new ‘Horizon Europe 2028-2034’ programme. Greek universities and research centres are being transformed into branches of the war industry: the research centres ‘Demokritos’, ‘CERTH’ and ‘FORTH’ are participating in the NATO DIANA programme; we have the NTUA involved in 21 projects for military purposes funded by the EDF and ‘Horizon Europe’; the ‘UnderSec’ programme in which the University of West Attica and the Hellenic Mediterranean University are collaborating with the Israeli Ministry of Defence; and the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki and Panteion taking on the role of war propagandist. In view of the above: 1.

What is the Commission's position on the fact that the shift to a war economy and the Preparedness Union are turning infrastructure and human knowledge into a pawn of imperialist competition, aligning the funding of research and scientific programmes with the pursuit of strengthening the EU's war industry, while cutting back on research in areas that could substantially improve the living conditions of the people?

What is the Commission’s position on the request to disengage universities and research centres from war preparations, by stopping all military war programmes and ensuring state funding for research focused on the needs of the people?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.7.2026) Horizon Europe1 is an over EUR 90 billion programme which covers vast areas of research and innovation, for example in clean transition and decarbonisation, digital transition, health, biotech, agriculture and bioeconomy. The Commission remains strongly committed to the funding of these priorities, through the specific programme implementing Horizon Europe2. This funding is not affected in any way by the support provided by the specific programme for defence research (the European Defence Fund3) which funds only activities with an exclusive focus on defence applications. As outlined in the Preparedness Union4 and ProtectEU Strategies5, reaching defence readiness requires a whole-of-society approach. Accordingly, civilian research institutions can play an important role in the pursuit of civilian preparedness. Furthermore, investments in defence research and development have positive spillover effects for the EU economy, boosting competitiveness, increasing the gross domestic product, and fostering innovation in critical sectors beyond defence, such as healthcare, energy and transport. This is also in the interest of European citizens.
